NASA is officially seeking rescue missions to save the Hubble Space Telescope before atmospheric drag pulls it to its doom. Hubble lacks thrusters, so upper atmospheric friction is continuously degrading its orbit. Without a boost, the twelve-ton observatory will eventually re-enter at seventeen thousand miles per hour. While friction would vaporize most of it into a blazing fireball, dense titanium structural brackets and its primary mirror support would survive impact. Should we spend millions to save Hubble, or let it burn? Follow for more what-ifs.

Based on today's news: Once again, NASA is asking for ideas to rescue Hubble from certain death
